facts.statement: The genus Rhaeticosaurus was named by Wintrich and colleagues in 2017.
The type species of the genus is Rhaeticosaurus mertensi.
Rhaeticosaurus, meaning 'Rhaetian lizard', is an extinct basal pliosauroid found in Late Triassic rocks of the Exter Formation.
facts.quote: Rhaeticosaurus (meaning 'Rhaetian lizard') is an extinct genus of basal pliosauroid from the Late Triassic (Rhaetian) rocks of the Exter Formation.

facts.statement: The only known species, R. mertensi, was named by Wintrich et al. in 2017.
facts.quote: The type and only species, R. mertensi, was named by Wintrich et al. in 2017.

facts.statement: The animal is known from a partial articulated skeleton.
facts.quote: It is known from a partial articulated skeleton.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen is cataloged as LWL-MFN P 64047.
The fossil was discovered in 2013 in Clay pit #3, which belonged to the Lücking brick company.
facts.quote: It was discovered in Clay pit #3 belonging to the Lücking brick company in 2013

facts.statement: The discovery site was located about 3.5 meters below a bonebed containing Rhaetian-age vertebrate fauna.
facts.quote: about 3.5 m below a bonebed containing a vertebrate fauna of Rhaetian age

facts.statement: Based on the holotype, Rhaeticosaurus reached a maximum length of 2.37 meters when fully grown.
facts.quote: Based on the holotype, Rhaeticosaurus grew up to 2.37 m when fully grown.

facts.statement: Rhaeticosaurus lived during the Rhaetian stage, between 205.7 and 201.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Rhaetian to Rhaetian (205.7 to 201.4 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The specimen was acquired by an anonymous private collector who notified authorities, leading to its preparation and naming in 2017.
rejected.quote: It was acquired by an anonymous private collector, who notified authorities and the specimen was eventually prepared and named as Rhaeticosaurus mertensi in 2017.
